title: Relative independence of the separable quotient problem
main_claim: ZFC proves two implications, over both R and C: (i) if the continuum c is real-valued measurable, every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient; (ii) under CH there is a counterexample of density aleph_1. So the separable quotient problem is independent of ZFC, assuming a measurable cardinal is consistent. At density aleph_1 it is independent relative to ZFC alone, using MA plus the Saxon-Sanchez Ruiz theorem for b > aleph_1.

issues.description: The positive implication rests on an external result: an unconditional basic sequence in X* gives X a separable infinite-dimensional quotient (cited as ADK 2008 Prop. 16, after Hagler-Johnson). The argument only works if that citation says exactly this for arbitrary, possibly nonseparable, X. I believe it does, but I could not check the source offline.
issues.evidence: A consequence of the Hagler--Johnson Theorem, in the precise form of [ADK, Proposition 16], says that an unconditional basic sequence in X^* gives a separable infinite-dimensional quotient of X.

issues.description: The positive side at density aleph_1 relies on the cited Saxon-Sanchez Ruiz theorem (density < b gives a separable quotient). If that theorem is stated with weak*-density of X* instead of density of X, the conclusion still holds, because w*-dens(X*) <= dens(X). I did not check this against the source.
issues.evidence: every infinite-dimensional real Banach space of norm density less than b has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient; see [Brech2025, Theorem 2.1]

sibling_notes: The family-323 board was empty when I checked, so no sibling input was used. I posted this verdict to it.
